title: TypeScript Introduction
summary: TypeScript adds labels called types to JavaScript. Those labels help find some mistakes before a program runs.
introduction: Imagine a box labelled "pencils". The label helps you notice if someone puts a book in it. A TypeScript type works a little like that label. It says what kind of value we expect. Learn the JavaScript basics first, then use this lesson to meet three simple types.
learningObjectives: Explain why a type is like a label
Use number, string and boolean types
Explain why types do not check outside data by themselves

blocks.text: The part `: number` is a **type label**. It tells TypeScript that `pencils` should hold a number. The rest looks like JavaScript because TypeScript builds on JavaScript.

blocks.title: A mistake for the checker to find

blocks.text: This example has a deliberate error. `"five"` is text, called a **string**. It does not match the `number` label. The TypeScript checker reports a type error. Change `"five"` to `5` to fix it.

blocks.title: Text, a number and a yes-or-no choice

blocks.text: What happens before the code runs?

A tool called `tsc` checks your TypeScript and can turn it into JavaScript. The type labels are left out of that JavaScript. A browser runs the JavaScript. This site shows TypeScript examples, but does not run them. The next lesson helps you set up the tools.

The labels help while you write code. They do not check new information that arrives later. For example, a file might be missing a person's age. Your running program still needs to check that the age is there.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: TypeScript finds many type mix-ups, but not every bug. A program can use the right types and still give the wrong answer. Read the result and test your code too.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Write down a type for each value: `"blue"`, `12`, and `false`. Then change the first example to count 8 pencils. What number should it show?

seo.title: TypeScript Introduction – Why Types Catch Bugs Early
seo.description: Learn what TypeScript is, how the compiler checks your code and erases the types, and why a type error in the editor beats a TypeError in production.
